tool.name: ITS-FUN-2-MAP
tool.description: extract and validate fungal ITS barcodes from museum genome skims
tool.command:
## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Working layout. Directory and file names mirror run_pipeline.sh exactly: ## itsfun-summary discovers its inputs by name (**/blast_*summary.csv etc.). ## --------------------------------------------------------------------------- mkdir -p reads db out/00_logs out/01_fastp_processed out/02_UNITEd out/03_mapped_reads out/04_assemblies out/05_blast_round1 out/05a_blast_parsed1 out/06_blast_round2a-ITS2 out/06a_blast_parsed2a-ITS2 out/07_blast_round2b-ITS1 out/07a_blast_parsed2b-ITS1 out/08_its_primer_extraction &&
## Stage reads under neutral names; the tracking sheet carries the mapping ## from sample ID to file, so filenames never need to match IDs. #for $i, $pair in enumerate($reads): #set $ext = 'fastq.gz' if $pair.forward.ext.endswith('.gz') else 'fastq' ln -s '$pair.forward' 'reads/r${i}_R1.${ext}' && ln -s '$pair.reverse' 'reads/r${i}_R2.${ext}' && #end for
## Reference databases: symlink into a writable directory so makeblastdb ## can write its index files next to the FASTA. ln -s '$databases.unite_full' db/unite_full.fasta && ln -s '$databases.unite_general' db/unite_general.fasta && ln -s '$databases.uchime_its2' db/uchime_its2.fasta && ln -s '$databases.uchime_its1' db/uchime_its1.fasta &&
## Build a clean CSV tracking sheet with forward/reverse paths injected. python '$__tool_directory__/prepare_sheet.py' '$tracking_sheet' '$tracking_sheet.ext' $sheet_index '$column_name' '$pairs_tsv' tracking.csv &&
#if $taxonomy.source == 'ncbi': itsfun-lineage --input_csv tracking.csv --output_csv tracking_lineage.csv --email '$__user_email__' --taxcolumn '$taxid_column' --log_file out/00_logs/pull_ncbi_lineage.log && test -s tracking_lineage.csv && #set $sheet = 'tracking_lineage.csv' #else: #set $sheet = 'tracking.csv' #end if
## Step 1: quality control itsfun-qc --output_dir out/01_fastp_processed --tracking_sheet $sheet --column_name '$column_name' --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --fastp_threads 1 --qualified_quality_phred $qc.qualified_quality_phred --log_file out/00_logs/fastp.log &&
## Step 2: pseudo-reference retrieval from UNITE itsfun-refs --tracking_sheet $sheet --unite_db db/unite_full.fasta --output out/02_UNITEd --email '$__user_email__' --id_header '$column_name' --taxid_header '$taxid_column' --tax_rank $refs.tax_rank #if $refs.selection.mode == 'number': --number $refs.selection.number #if $refs.selection.traverse != 'none': --traverse $refs.selection.traverse #end if $refs.selection.diversity #else: --all #end if --summary_csv UNITEd_summary.csv --log_file out/00_logs/UNITEd.log &&
## Step 3: read mapping and baiting itsfun-map --input_dir out/01_fastp_processed --ref_dir out/02_UNITEd --aligner $mapping.aligner --output_dir out/03_mapped_reads --tracking_sheet $sheet --column_name '$column_name' --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --bwa_threads 1 --log_file out/00_logs/mapping.log &&
## Step 4: contig assembly itsfun-assemble --merged_dir out/03_mapped_reads --unmerged_dir out/01_fastp_processed --output_dir out/04_assemblies --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --k '$assembly.kmers' --summary_csv out/04_assemblies/assembly_summary.csv --log_file out/00_logs/assembly.log &&
## Step 5: BLASTn round 1 against the UNITE general release itsfun-blast1 --query_dir out/04_assemblies --database_file db/unite_general.fasta --makeblastdb --output_dir out/05_blast_round1 --tracking_sheet $sheet --column_name '$column_name' --max_workers \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --evalue $blast.evalue --log_file out/00_logs/blast_round1.log &&
## Step 5.5: round 1 parsing and taxonomic validation itsfun-blast1-parse --input_dir out/05_blast_round1 --output_dir out/05a_blast_parsed1 --taxonomy_csv $sheet --id_column '$column_name' --min_len $blast.min_len --min_pident $blast.min_pident --evalue_cutoff $blast.evalue_cutoff --assembly_dir out/04_assemblies $blast.allow_all --log_file out/00_logs/parse_round1.log &&
## Step 6: BLASTn round 2a against UCHIME ITS2 itsfun-blast2 --query_dir out/04_assemblies --blast_dir out/05_blast_round1 --database_file db/uchime_its2.fasta --makeblastdb --output_dir out/06_blast_round2a-ITS2 --tracking_sheet $sheet --column_name '$column_name' --max_workers \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --evalue $blast.evalue --log_file out/00_logs/blast_round2a.log &&
## Step 6.5: ITS2 parsing and validation itsfun-blast-parse --input_dir out/06_blast_round2a-ITS2 --output_dir out/06a_blast_parsed2a-ITS2 --min_len $blast.min_len --min_pident $blast.min_pident --taxonomy_csv $sheet --assembly_dir out/04_assemblies --id_column '$column_name' --summary_csv out/06a_blast_parsed2a-ITS2/blast_parser_its2_summary.csv --log_file out/00_logs/parse_round2a.log &&
## Step 7: BLASTn round 2b against UCHIME ITS1 itsfun-blast2 --query_dir out/04_assemblies --blast_dir out/05_blast_round1 --database_file db/uchime_its1.fasta --makeblastdb --output_dir out/07_blast_round2b-ITS1 --tracking_sheet $sheet --column_name '$column_name' --max_workers \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} --evalue $blast.evalue --log_file out/00_logs/blast_round2b.log &&
## Step 7.5: ITS1 parsing and validation itsfun-blast-parse --input_dir out/07_blast_round2b-ITS1 --output_dir out/07a_blast_parsed2b-ITS1 --min_len $blast.min_len --min_pident $blast.min_pident --taxonomy_csv $sheet --assembly_dir out/04_assemblies --id_column '$column_name' --summary_csv out/07a_blast_parsed2b-ITS1/blast_parser_its1_summary.csv --log_file out/00_logs/parse_round2b.log &&
## Step 8: primer binding and ITS extraction itsfun-extract --input out/06a_blast_parsed2a-ITS2 --tracking_sheet $sheet --column_name '$column_name' --output out/08_its_primer_extraction #if $primers.source == 'custom': --primers_tsv '$primers.primers_tsv' --regions_tsv '$primers.regions_tsv' #end if --log_file out/00_logs/primer_binding.log &&
## Step 9: summary, decision making and final FASTAs itsfun-summary out -o merged_summary.csv --log out/00_logs/merge_outputs.log --delim '$summary.delim' #if $summary.naming_tsv: --naming_tsv '$summary.naming_tsv' #end if
#if $extra_outputs and 'summaries' in $extra_outputs: && mkdir -p step_summaries && find out -name '*_summary.csv' -not -path 'out/final_results_dir/*' -exec cp {} step_summaries/ \; && if [ -f out/08_its_primer_extraction/summary_report.txt ]; then cp out/08_its_primer_extraction/summary_report.txt step_summaries/; fi #end if #if $extra_outputs and 'scaffolds' in $extra_outputs: && mkdir -p scaffolds_out && for d in out/04_assemblies/*.spades.out; do if [ -s "\$d/scaffolds.fasta" ]; then cp "\$d/scaffolds.fasta" "scaffolds_out/\$(basename "\$d" .spades.out).fasta"; fi; done #end if

configfiles.configfile: #for $i, $pair in enumerate($reads): #set $ext = 'fastq.gz' if $pair.forward.ext.endswith('.gz') else 'fastq' ${pair.name} reads/r${i}_R1.${ext} reads/r${i}_R2.${ext} #end for

param.name: reads
param.label: Paired-end genome skim reads
param.help: One pair per specimen. Each element identifier must match a sample ID in the tracking sheet.

param.name: tracking_sheet
param.label: Tracking sheet
param.help: One row per specimen, with a sample ID column and an NCBI taxid column. Any forward/reverse file path columns are ignored.

validator.message: Use letters, digits and underscores only
Use letters, digits and underscores only

param.name: sheet_index
param.label: Sheet index (XLSX only)
param.help: 0 is the first sheet. Ignored for CSV and tabular input.

param.name: source
param.label: Taxonomic lineage for validation
param.option: Tracking sheet already has Kingdom to Species columns
Look up lineages from the taxids at NCBI

param.label: Phred score below which a base counts as unqualified
Move up to this rank if too few sequences are found
Spread sequences across child taxa
param.help: Prioritises target species matches (up to 25% of the total), then distributes the rest across other child taxa.

param.name: kmers
param.label: k-mer sizes
param.help: Comma-separated odd integers for the initial assembly attempt. The fallback attempts always use k=21.

param.label: E-value cutoff when parsing round 1 hits
Let multiple matching contigs pass round 1
param.help: As in the reference run_pipeline.sh. Without this, a specimen with more than one matching contig fails round 1.

param.name: source
param.label: ITS primers
param.option: White et al. (1990) ITS1 to ITS4

param.name: primers_tsv
param.label: Primers
param.help: Tab-separated with a header row: name, sequence.

param.name: regions_tsv
param.label: Regions
param.help: Tab-separated with a header row: region, forward, reverse. Primer names must match the primers table.

param.label: Renaming table
param.help: Optional. Two tab-separated columns without a header: sample ID and new name for the output FASTA.

param.name: extra_outputs
param.label: Additional outputs
param.option: Extracted ITS1, ITS2 and complete ITS sequences

tool.help:
**What it does**
ITS-FUN-2-MAP recovers fungal ITS barcodes from low-coverage genome skims of museum and herbarium specimens. It runs the complete pipeline in one job:
1. Quality control, adapter trimming and read merging (fastp) 2. Retrieval of taxonomically matched pseudo-references from UNITE, using each specimen's NCBI taxid 3. Read baiting by mapping to those references (BWA-MEM, or BWA-ALN with ancient DNA settings) 4. Assembly of the baited reads (SPAdes, with two fallback strategies) 5. BLASTn of scaffolds against the UNITE general release, and validation against the expected taxonomy 6. BLASTn of validated contigs against UCHIME ITS2 and ITS1 references, with a second round of validation 7. ITS1, ITS2 and complete ITS extraction by primer binding (seqkit amplicon) 8. A merged summary across all steps, a final decision per specimen, and renamed FASTAs ready for submission
-----
**Inputs**
*Reads*: a list of paired collections of FASTQ files, one pair per specimen. **Each element identifier must exactly match a sample ID in the tracking sheet**, and may only contain letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens.
Several steps match files to samples by substring, so the tool refuses to run if one sample ID occurs inside another (for example S1 and S10). Zero-padded IDs (S01, S10) avoid this.
*Tracking sheet*: CSV, tab-separated or XLSX, one row per specimen. It needs:
- a sample ID column (default ``ID``) - an NCBI taxid column (default ``taxid``) - for validation, the columns ``Kingdom``, ``Phylum``, ``Class``, ``Order``, ``Family``, ``Genus`` and ``Species``, unless you let the tool look lineages up at NCBI
Rows without matching reads are skipped. Any ``forward``/``reverse`` file path columns are ignored, because Galaxy supplies the reads.
*Reference databases*: four FASTA files from the UNITE repository (https://unite.ut.ee/repository.php): the full UNITE+INSD release, the general release (dynamic species hypotheses), and the UCHIME ITS2 and ITS1 reference datasets. BLAST indexes are built during the run.
-----
**Outputs**
- *Summary*: one row per specimen with metrics from every step and the final outcome (``Final_outcome``, ``Final_contig_desc``, ``Final_contig``) - *Passed barcodes*: FASTA per specimen that passed all validation, with headers of the form ``<ID>|<region>`` - *Needs manual verification*: FASTA per specimen where the evidence was ambiguous
Optionally also the extracted ITS1, ITS2 and complete ITS sequences, the per-step summary tables, the assembled scaffolds and the per-step logs.
-----
**Notes**
- The pseudo-reference step and the optional lineage lookup query NCBI Entrez using the email address of your Galaxy account. Jobs therefore need outbound internet access. - The defaults follow the authors' reference script ``run_pipeline.sh``. - Memory use is dominated by SPAdes. The authors report a run of 108 specimens in about 2.3 hours with 24 CPUs and 150 GB of memory.
Source code: https://github.com/museomics/its-fun-2-map
